<STRUCT_0001>
This chapter develops formal deformation theory in a form applicable
later in the Stacks project, closely following Rim <REF_0001>
and Schlessinger <REF_0002>. We strongly encourage the reader new to
this topic to read the paper by Schlessinger first, as it is sufficiently
general for most applications, and Schlessinger's results are indeed
used in most papers that use this kind of formal deformation theory.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Let <MATH_0001> be a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field <MATH_0002>,
and let <MATH_0003> denote the category of Artinian local
<MATH_0004>-algebras with residue field <MATH_0005>. Given a functor
<MATH_0006> such that <MATH_0007>
is a one element set, Schlessinger's paper introduced conditions
(H1)-(H4) such that:
<STRUCT_0004>
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0008> has a ``hull'' if and only if (H1)-(H3) hold.
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0009> is prorepresentable if and only if (H1)-(H4) hold.
<STRUCT_0007>
The purpose of this chapter is to generalize these results in two ways
exactly as is done in Rim's paper:
<STRUCT_0008>
<ITEMOPEN_0001>(A)<ITEMCLOSE_0001> The functor <MATH_0010> is replaced by a category <MATH_0011> cofibered
in groupoids over <MATH_0012>, see
Section <REF_0003>.
<ITEMOPEN_0002>(B)<ITEMCLOSE_0002> We let <MATH_0013> be a Noetherian ring and <MATH_0014>
a finite ring map to a field. The category <MATH_0015> is
the category of Artinian local <MATH_0016>-algebras <MATH_0017> endowed with a
given identification <MATH_0018>.
<STRUCT_0009>
The analogue of the condition that <MATH_0019> is a  one element set is that
<MATH_0020> is the trivial groupoid. If <MATH_0021> satisfies this
condition then we say it is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>predeformation category<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>, but in  general
we do not make this assumption.  Rim's paper <REF_0004> is the
original source for the results in this document. We also mention the useful
paper <REF_0005>, which discusses deformation theory with groupoids
but in less generality than we do here.

<STRUCT_0010><STRUCT_0011>
An important role is played by the ``completion''
<MATH_0022> of the category <MATH_0023>.
An object of <MATH_0024> is a Noetherian complete
local <MATH_0025>-algebra <MATH_0026> whose residue field is identified with <MATH_0027>, see
Section <REF_0006>.
On the one hand <MATH_0028>
is a strictly full subcategory and on the other hand
<MATH_0029> is a full subcategory of the category
of pro-objects of <MATH_0030>. A functor
<MATH_0031> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>prorepresentable<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>
if it is isomorphic to the restriction of a representable functor
<MATH_0032>
to <MATH_0033> where
<MATH_0034>.

<STRUCT_0012><STRUCT_0013>
<TEXTITOPEN_0003>Categories cofibred in groupoids<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> are dual to categories fibred in
groupoids; we introduce them in Section <REF_0007>.
A <TEXTITOPEN_0004>smooth<TEXTITCLOSE_0004> morphism of categories cofibred in groupoids over
<MATH_0035> is one that satisfies the infinitesimal lifting
criterion for objects, see
Section <REF_0008>.
This is analogous to the definition of a formally smooth ring map, see
Algebra, Definition <REF_0009>
and is exactly dual to the notion in
Criteria for Representability, Section <REF_0010>.
This is an important notion as we eventually want to prove that certain
kinds of categories cofibred in groupoids have a smooth prorepresentable
presentation, much like the characterization of algebraic stacks in
Algebraic Stacks, Sections <REF_0011> and
<REF_0012>.
A <TEXTITOPEN_0005>versal formal object<TEXTITCLOSE_0005> of a category <MATH_0036> cofibred
in groupoids over <MATH_0037> is an object
<MATH_0038> of the completion such that the
associated morphism
<MATH_0039>
is smooth.

<STRUCT_0014><STRUCT_0015>
In
Section <REF_0013>,
we define conditions (S1) and (S2) on <MATH_0040> generalizing
Schlessinger's (H1) and (H2). The analogue of Schlessinger's
(H3)---the condition that <MATH_0041> has finite dimensional
tangent space---is not given a name.
A key step in the development of the theory is the existence of
versal formal objects for predeformation categories satisfying
(S1), (S2) and (H3), see
Lemma <REF_0014>.
Schlessinger's notion of a <TEXTITOPEN_0006>hull<TEXTITCLOSE_0006> for a functor
<MATH_0042>
is, in our terminology, a versal formal object <MATH_0043>
such that the induced map of tangent spaces
<MATH_0044>
is an isomorphism.
In the literature a hull is often called a ``miniversal'' object.
We do not do so, and here is why. It can happen that a functor has a
versal formal object without having a hull. Moreover, we show in
Section <REF_0015>
that if a predeformation category has a versal formal object, then
it always has a <TEXTITOPEN_0007>minimal<TEXTITCLOSE_0007> one (as defined in
Definition <REF_0016>)
which is unique up to isomorphism, see
Lemma <REF_0017>.
But it can happen that the minimal versal formal object does not
induce an isomorphism on tangent spaces! (See
Examples <REF_0018> and
<REF_0019>.)

<STRUCT_0016><STRUCT_0017>
Keeping in mind the differences pointed out above,
Theorem <REF_0020>
is the direct generalization of (1) above: it recovers Schlessinger's
result in the case that <MATH_0045> is a functor and it characterizes
minimal versal formal objects, in the presence of conditions
(S1) and (S2), in terms of the map
<MATH_0046>
on tangent spaces.

<STRUCT_0018><STRUCT_0019>
In Section <REF_0021>,
we define Rim's condition (RS) on <MATH_0047> generalizing
Schlessinger's (H4). A <TEXTITOPEN_0008>deformation category<TEXTITCLOSE_0008> is defined as a
predeformation category satisfying (RS).
The analogue to prorepresentable functors are the categories
cofibred in groupoids over <MATH_0048> which have
a <TEXTITOPEN_0009>presentation by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors<TEXTITCLOSE_0009>
on <MATH_0049>, see
Definitions <REF_0022>,
<REF_0023>, and
<REF_0024>.
This notion of a presentation takes into account the groupoid structure
of the fibers of <MATH_0050>. In
Theorem <REF_0025>
we prove that <MATH_0051> has a presentation by a smooth prorepresentable
groupoid in functors if and only if <MATH_0052> has a finite dimensional
tangent space and finite dimensional infinitesimal automorphism space.
This is the generalization of (2) above: it reduces to Schlessinger's result
in the case that <MATH_0053> is a functor.
There is a final
Section <REF_0026>
where we discuss how to use minimal versal formal objects
to produce a (unique up to isomorphism) minimal presentation
by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors.

<STRUCT_0020><STRUCT_0021>
We also find the following conceptual explanation for Schlessinger's
conditions. If a predeformation category <MATH_0054> satisfies (RS),
then the associated functor of isomorphism classes
<MATH_0055>
satisfies (H1) and (H2)
(Lemmas <REF_0027> and
<REF_0028>).
Conversely, if a functor
<MATH_0056>
arises naturally as the functor of isomorphism classes of
a category <MATH_0057> cofibered in groupoids, then it seems to happen in
practice that an argument showing <MATH_0058> satisfies (H1) and (H2) will also show
<MATH_0059> satisfies (RS). Examples are discussed in
Deformation Problems, Section
<REF_0029>.
Moreover, if <MATH_0060> satisfies (RS), then condition
(H4) for <MATH_0061> has a simple interpretation in terms of
extending automorphisms of objects of <MATH_0062>
(Lemma <REF_0030>).
These observations suggest that (RS) should be regarded as the
fundamental deformation theoretic glueing condition.
